claims.text: No repository uses Databricks or a database, and the tool view says no Databricks or other workspace is used by ap_pipeline, so Databricks access is not applicable.
Repository ap_pipeline (Python 3.9, standard library) is available locally and the agent identity has write access; git status is clean.
Branch feature/story was created from dev at 3fcbe1b and is checked out (HEAD holds ref: refs/heads/feature/story).
Branches main and dev both hold commit 3fcbe1bad11e1fb6b44523c7ca795d0c1ca7b1d8.
The Data Engineering tasks in scope are TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02), both on ap_pipeline, so no new repository is needed.
The CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py with a coverage gate of 90% and static checks for print/eval/exec, bare except and lines longer than 140 characters.
ap_pipeline is at version 0.4.0 and TSK-01 owns the version step.
ci.py imports the third-party coverage package, while the repository memory states Python 3.9 (standard library).
.git/config sets an upstream only for main and dev; remote origin is https://github.com/arghya05/ap-pipeline-sample.git.
schedule.json sets a daily run at 02:00, timezone Asia/Kolkata, and is on TSK-01's must-not-change list.

open_questions: RA-1 (non-blocking): The feature branch is named feature/story rather than feature/<story>. Should both Data Engineering stories (STORY-01, STORY-02) share it? Interim: yes, with story-ID commit prefixes.
RA-2 (non-blocking): This step could not confirm that the coverage package that ci.py needs is installed for /usr/bin/python3, because shell commands are not allowed here.
RA-3 (non-blocking): feature/story has no upstream configured and this step did not test a push. Write access rests on the tool view, and the spine pushes at DE-10.
